content.title: Single standard deduction recalculates live and shows the ordered estimate breakdown
content.intent: Prove the calculator recalculates live without submit or reload and presents the ordered estimate breakdown, gross income echo, Single standard deduction, and an allowed total label.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning with the PRD's representative annual income 85000 and filing status Single. Applied state/flow to cover live recalculation while typing. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was used: filing status and deduction type change expected outcomes and were split into separate scenarios. Negative validation, i18n, a11y, and responsiveness were not minted because this calculator source states no such promises and localization/mobile are explicit non-goals.

content.title: Taxable income stays at $0 when gross income is at or below the Single standard deduction
content.intent: Prove taxable income never drops below zero when gross income does not exceed the active deduction.
content.technique_notes: Applied boundary value analysis to the floor-at-zero rule using the authority expansion around the Single deduction threshold 14600: 0, 14599, 14600, 14601. Kept the zero-outcome representatives 0, 14599, and 14600 in this one scenario because they are equivalent for the expected result; split 14601 into a separate scenario because it changes the outcome. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was used because this is a one-input boundary around a specified threshold.

content.title: Taxable income becomes $1 immediately above the Single standard deduction boundary
content.intent: Prove the taxable-income calculation crosses from zero to a positive whole-dollar amount immediately above the deduction threshold.
content.technique_notes: Applied boundary value analysis to the floor-at-zero rule and isolated 14601 from the authority expansion around 14600 because the expected taxable income changes from zero to positive. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was used because this is a single boundary-crossing check on one calculation input.

content.title: Married filing jointly updates the standard deduction to $29,200
content.intent: Prove choosing Married filing jointly changes the Deductions row to the married standard deduction amount.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning with a representative positive annual income of 85000 so the estimate panel is populated while isolating the filing-status effect. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was used because each filing status produces a distinct required deduction amount and therefore became its own scenario.

content.title: Head of household updates the standard deduction to $21,900
content.intent: Prove choosing Head of household changes the Deductions row to the head-of-household standard deduction amount.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning with a representative positive annual income of 85000 so the estimate panel is populated while isolating the filing-status effect. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was used because each filing status produces a distinct required deduction amount and therefore became its own scenario.

content.title: Selecting Itemized reveals the itemized deductions input
content.intent: Prove choosing Itemized exposes the itemized deductions input control.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning with a representative populated state and isolated deduction-type switching because it changes the visible controls rather than a numeric amount stated by the PRD. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because the calculator is money-related, but no covering array was used because the only outcome-changing variable under test here is deduction type.
